label: Real run on this Mac's Docker Compose stack, with synthetic traffic from klaxon.traffic: synthetic data, a simulated provider, no real money. One fault from klaxon.faults, secret-rotation, was injected on purpose. The alert was raised by klaxon.alerts from what the stack showed. Klaxon's loop ran live on it, through Claude Code on Aravind's seat, and stopped on diagnosed after 7 steps; any reply it got is a recorded response, not a simulation. It was offered one write action (rollback_deploy), as in week 4; in an evaluation run its gate only plans an action the diagnosis names: nobody is asked, and nothing runs. The diagnosis was compared with the fault's recorded cause by a rule (klaxon.grading), not by a person or a model. Code planned the action its diagnosis named (redeploy webhook-receiver: WEBHOOK_SECRET_VERSION v2 -> v1); in an evaluation run nobody is asked, and nothing ran. The fault's cause was removed by the harness's clearing (klaxon.faults).

case.name: secret-rotation
case.title: The books stop catching up: our webhook receiver refuses every webhook
case.right_answer: The fault's recorded cause: a deploy of the webhook receiver with a rotated secret the provider does not sign with (WEBHOOK_SECRET_VERSION=v2, while the provider signs with v1): every webhook fails its signature check and is refused with a 400, so no event reaches Kafka, and the provider keeps sending them again, with backoff.
case.remedy: roll the webhook receiver back to v1 (or accept both versions until the provider signs with v2): the provider sends every refused webhook again, and the books catch up by themselves

expected_symptoms: the books cannot catch up with the provider: the money check cannot settle, the provider's webhooks not acknowledged, and the books rule fires at its second evaluation, about 50 s after the deploy
the receiver refuses every webhook with a 400, counts it as bad_signature and logs 'webhook refused: bad signature'; the provider sends its growing backlog again and again, tens of times a second
nothing new is booked or confirmed, and both consumers' lag stays at 0: nothing reaches Kafka

payments and refunds still go through, but one whose answer was lost cannot be confirmed: its client's retries get 503 again, so the 5xx share of POST /payments about doubles and its p95 climbs to about 0.6 s, both under their thresholds

after the rollback the books catch up within about three minutes: the provider sends each refused webhook again within a minute of its last try, and one whose acknowledgement is then lost (the traffic's noise) a minute later
fault.remedy: roll the webhook receiver back to v1 (or accept both versions until the provider signs with v2): the provider sends every refused webhook again, and the books catch up by themselves

alert.name: BooksBehindProvider
alert.summary: Our books cannot catch up with the provider: at each of the last 2 evaluations, the money check waited 15 s and could not settle up to its cutoff. At the last one, 155 of the provider's webhooks up to it had not been acknowledged yet.

diagnosis.hypothesis: The webhook-receiver was redeployed at 10:59:00Z with WEBHOOK_SECRET_VERSION=v2. The provider still signs its webhooks with the previous secret, so the receiver now refuses every one with HTTP 400 'signature mismatch' and queues nothing to provider-events. The provider gets no acknowledgement, so it keeps resending. The refusal rate (~22/s) is far above the earlier acceptance rate (~3/s), which fits a pile of retries. Unacknowledged webhooks keep growing, so the ledger and confirmer cannot catch up and the money check cannot settle to its cutoff. That is the BooksBehindProvider alert, with 155 unacknowledged webhooks. Open questions: I did not see the provider's secret version directly. The mismatch is inferred from the timing and the refusal reason. I also did not run money_check myself, but c6 confirms the symptom: zero webhooks queued since about 10:59:40.

evidence.shows: All containers are healthy. webhook-receiver alone was recreated, at 10:59:00Z, about a minute before the alert.
The webhook-receiver deploy at 10:59:00Z set WEBHOOK_SECRET_VERSION=v2. No other service changed after 10:57:22.
Every recent webhook-receiver request on /webhooks/provider returns 400 with the warning 'webhook refused: bad signature', reason 'signature mismatch'.
Queued webhooks ran at ~3/s until 10:59 and then fell to zero (the series ends at 10:59:36). bad_signature appears from 10:59:21 and climbs to ~22/s as the provider retries.
Total webhook receipts climb steeply after 10:59, a sign of provider retries against a receiver that never acknowledges.

proposed_fix.summary: Roll webhook-receiver back to its settings before the 10:59:00 deploy, i.e. the previous WEBHOOK_SECRET_VERSION that matches the provider's signing secret. The provider retries until it gets an acknowledgement, so the refused webhooks should be redelivered and queued. The idempotent ledger and confirmer then catch up. Afterwards, run money_check with wait=true to confirm everything settles. Re-attempt the v2 secret rotation only once the provider signs with v2, or once the receiver accepts both versions.

diagnosis.blast_radius: webhook-receiver is recreated and pauses briefly. Webhooks sent during the restart go unacknowledged and are retried, the same as now. Once it is back, a burst of retried webhooks arrives, raising Kafka and consumer load and lag for a while. Duplicates are safe because ledger-consumer is idempotent and confirmer matches by our id. If the provider has actually switched to v2 for some events, those would start failing instead, but the c6 data shows the old secret was working until the deploy.
diagnosis.rollback_plan: If the rollback makes things worse, redeploy webhook-receiver with WEBHOOK_SECRET_VERSION=v2, the current state. Then coordinate the secret rotation with the provider instead.
